A few people asked why my latest book focuses on Elijah. Shouldn’t we as believers focus on Jesus?
Consider this. When Jesus was transfigured in glory on the mountain, His face shining like the sun, who did the Father send to stand with Him? Moses and Elijah. The Law and the Prophets, standing on either side of the Messiah. In Matthew 17:3, we read that “Moses and Elijah appeared to them, talking with Him.” That is not a small detail. Of all the giants in Israel’s history, Elijah is chosen to represent every prophet who ever spoke for God.

And the record goes further. When the crowds tried to guess who Jesus was, many of them said, “He is Elijah.” When Jesus spoke of John the Baptist, He said John came in the spirit and power of Elijah. The very last verse of the Old Testament, in Malachi, promised that God will send Elijah before the great and dreadful day of the Lord.

So Elijah stands at both ends of the story. He points forward to John, who prepared the way for the first coming, and he points forward again to the days before the second coming. This man is woven right through the ministry of Jesus from beginning to end. 

Once I saw how deeply connected they were, I could not read his story the same way again. That connection is at the heart of ‘The Elijah Mandate’.

So here’s my answer to the opening question: a deep study of the word of God and of the characters most pivotal to Jesus’ ministry are how we focus on Jesus. 

Pre-order ‘The Elijah Mandate’ today. Once you’ve read the book, you’ll not only know more about Elijah, you will see Jesus more clearly than you ever have. And every pre-order tells the bookstores the same thing God told Elijah on that mountain – there are far more of us around than the world thinks.

ONE BILL WILL NOT DEFINE THE ENTIRE MARKET.

The Crypto CLARITY Act remains one of the most important regulatory developments for the US digital asset industry.

The Senate Banking Committee advanced the legislation in May by a bipartisan 15–9 vote.

But the bill has not yet passed the full Senate and has not become law.

At the same time, the regulatory process is not standing still.

SEC Chair Paul Atkins has said that the Commission’s 2026 agenda includes:

• clearer rules for crypto capital formation
• bringing more digital asset products onshore
• custody guidance
• rules for trading tokenized securities onchain

This creates two parallel processes.

Congress can establish a permanent statutory framework and define agency authority.

Regulators can interpret existing laws and develop rules inside the authority they already have.

Those processes are connected.

They are not interchangeable.

Agency rulemaking cannot automatically replace legislation.

Legislation cannot implement itself without detailed regulatory work.

For digital asset companies, the important questions are therefore broader than:

“Will the CLARITY Act pass this week?”

They include:

• What rules are already changing?
• Which agency currently has authority?
• What requires new legislation?
• Which obligations will depend on future rulemaking?
• How long will implementation take after passage?

A headline can create momentum.

A functioning market structure requires:

- law

- rules

- implementation

- enforcement

Legislation defines the architecture.
Regulation turns it into an operating system.

🎙 Iran, Pakistan reaffirm $10bn trade goal, advance free trade agreement

📌 Islamabad, IRNA – Iran and Pakistan have signed a memorandum of understanding to expand bilateral trade, reaffirming their commitment to raising annual trade to $10 billion and advancing negotiations toward a free trade agreement.

The memorandum was signed during the closing session of the 10th Joint Trade Committee in Islamabad on Wednesday, attended by Iran’s Minister of Industry, Mine and Trade, Mohammad Atabak, and Pakistan’s Commerce Minister, Jam Kamal Khan.
​
The two sides discussed expanding commercial cooperation, particularly in shared border regions, developing maritime and shipping activities, coordinating steps toward a free trade agreement, establishing joint free trade zones, and promoting barter trade.
​
Atabak said negotiations over the past two days had focused on increasing commercial exchanges, adding that some areas required facilitation and the removal of obstacles, and that the Pakistani side agreed to pursue further follow-up.
​
He said key decisions included activating border regions, expanding cross-border trade, strengthening private-sector participation, exchanging technical delegations, and immediately implementing bilateral agreements.
​
“The Islamic Republic has no limitation on increasing the volume of trade with Pakistan,” Atabak said, calling on business communities in both countries to play a leading role.
​
A separate cooperation memorandum was also signed between the Iran Chamber of Commerce, Industries, Mines and Agriculture and the Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry.
​
Atabak is also scheduled to meet Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif during his visit.

The West has consistently sought to impose its self-constructed values of liberal democracy, masked as human rights, upon the world, while disregarding the rich culture of other nations, including Islamic countries, said the statement issued on Wednesday.
